result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and continuous sidewalks. However, the wide roadway and lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals or traffic calming measures like curb extensions increase the risk for people crossing.

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground corner near the brick building

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, which may lead to confusion or unsafe crossings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian signals with countdown timers to improve crossing safety.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway and to calm traffic.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalks and pedestrian signals. The environment is characterized by residential row houses and continuous sidewalks, though it lacks physical traffic calming features like curb extensions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked near the intersection corners can obstruct the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs near the crosswalks on both sides of the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and continuous sidewalks. However, the crossing distance remains relatively long without physical protection like curb extensions, and parked vehicles near the corner may obstruct sightlines.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk limit visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb on the right side, adjacent to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: The lack of curb extensions or a median refuge increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: The width of the roadway across the marked crosswalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light.
